claim: Many-pair translating telephones are commonly used.
originalWording: Many-pair translating telephones are commonly used.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Ordinary users have practical two-way spoken translation for many language pairs; no perfect all-language requirement.
reference.rationale: Jibbigo provided a real but limited 2009 translating-phone capability. It was not yet a routine many-pair service. Google’s 2011 and 2015 conversation/speech products establish the broader consumer capability by 2015. Accents and mistakes do not negate ordinary practical use.

evidence.title: Apple: Translate phone calls and conversations
evidence.note: Current iOS 26 guide lists one-on-one spoken Phone translation across English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese and Korean variants. Supports actual telephone integration, not perfect translation quality.. strict.criterion: Speech-to-speech translation is integrated into live telephone calls for many ordinary language pairs, without requiring all languages or flawless human equivalence.
strict.rationale: The 2009 product evidence was narrower. Apple documents spoken in-call translation shipping in September 2025, and its current guide lists multiple common languages. This satisfies practical telephone integration; perfect translation was not required.
